title: Raw Argo floats show a shared cold step of about 0.03 C near 2016 in four in situ-based SST products at 60S-60N that drifters and moorings do not have; DOISST warms 0.014 C per decade too fast
abstract: We used 1.38 million raw Argo profiles at a fixed depth of 5 dbar (60S-60N, 143 months of 2005-2025) as a stable reference for eight SST products. We sampled each product at each profile and calculated area-weighted monthly series of product minus Argo. Drifters (179,515 collocations) and tropical moorings (11,302 collocations) show that Argo is stable: trends of +0.006 and +0.003 C per decade and steps at 2016 of +0.005 and +0.006 C, all with intervals that include zero. Against Argo, 2005-2025 trends of product minus Argo are +0.014 C per decade for DOISST v2.1, +0.006 for ERSSTv6, -0.004 for HadSST4.2, -0.010 for ERSSTv5, -0.012 for ERA5, -0.022 for COBE-SST2, -0.026 for OI SST v2 and -0.032 for HadISST1. The negative values are mostly one shared step: the mean of COBE-SST2, HadISST1, HadSST4.2 and ERA5 minus Argo drops by 0.027 C (0.017 to 0.037) at January 2016 (blind best break October 2016, p = 0.002), and no trend remains after the step. The tests confirm the DOISST July 2020 step (+0.048 C) and the OI v2 July 2018 step (-0.054 C). They do not confirm the DOISST January 2016 step of the joint homogenisation (+0.001 C): the other products drop instead. They also do not confirm an ERA5 October 2020 step. Drifter manufacturers differ by up to 0.058 C, and the fleet became 0.017 C warmer, but this does not explain the product step. Argo near-surface sampling moved from 4.9 to 4.2 dbar, which adds 0.006 C of false warming if not corrected. Anchoring each product to Argo halves the spread of 2005-2022 trends (0.189 +/- 0.018 C per decade). The shared step lowers 1985-2024 trends that use these products by about 0.007 C per decade. Limitations: 143 of 252 months; three products ingest Argo; Argo-sparse areas are not tested; the cause of the 2016 step is not identified; the 2023/24 jump is not resolved.

display.caption: Annual mean of four in situ-based products (COBE-SST2, HadISST1, HadSST4.2, ERA5) minus raw Argo, with drifters minus Argo and moorings minus Argo, relative to 2005-2015 (left). Only the products drop after 2016. Right: drifter SST offsets by manufacturer against Argo.

citations.reason: Extends the raw-Argo, drifter and mooring method from the tropical Pacific to 60S-60N; global drifter manufacturer offsets agree with its values.

Against Argo, DOISST has no January 2016 step; the other products drop by about 0.03 C, so the joint search attributed a shared error to DOISST, and its consensus trend is probably about 0.007 C per decade too low. No ERA5 October 2020 step against Argo.
Measures a shared product error of about 0.03 C near 2016 with an independent reference, as that bound study required.
DOISST warms too fast against Argo (0.014 C per decade in 2005-2025), but by less than against in situ reconstructions, which warm too slowly after 2016.
Argo confirms the DOISST July 2020 warm step (+0.048 C, p = 0.002).
Argo confirms the OI SST v2 July 2018 cold step (-0.054 C, p = 0.024).
Against Argo the ERSSTv6 January 2017 step is +0.026 C (p = 0.06), smaller than against other products, partly because the other products drop in 2016.
Same ERSSTv6 2016-2017 step tested against Argo.
The 2023/24 jump is tested against Argo; Argo cannot separate the products at this precision.
Earlier ERA5 check against moorings; here ERA5 SST shares the 2016 product step against Argo.
